correctness.rationale: The source Dirichlet identity and Stirling generating function give an exact rational function with m−1 simple real poles and explicit nonzero residues. Uniform Bohr recurrence on Re(s)>1 (derived from absolute convergence and simultaneous finite-prime phase returns) plus Rouché produces the same unbounded vertical shift for every pole; uniform derivative convergence proves residue transport. Strict triangle inequality yields no nonreal pole on or right of r_m. Lowry-Duda Theorem 2 then proves Ω± after accounting for the unique real pole at r_m; partial summation independently prohibits any fixed power-saving bound. Both cited nonstandard analytic inputs and their conditions were inspected. The packaged verify.py independently checks 549 exact rational-series coefficients and 744 exact Dirichlet coefficients, not infinite pole claims.

value.rationale: The exact leading growth exponent and main asymptotic do not preclude power-saving errors. The result identifies a coherent simultaneous m−1-level near-real pole-and-residue structure and proves the sharp impossibility of any polynomially smaller remainder for each m≥3. This is a natural boundary in the analytic enumeration of additive tiling systems and supplies information not equivalent to the known real-pole constant. It is not a finite table, parameter renaming, or routine numerical improvement.
